chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ - لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ -

translations.en: Ali ibn Abi Hamza – may God curse him –

chunks.arabic_text: أَصْلُ الْوَقْفِ، وَأَشَدُّ الْخَلْقِ عَدَاوَةً لِلْوَلِيِّ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: the root of Waqf, the most intense of creation in enmity to the Wali after Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* identifies ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamza as the progenitor of the Waqifiyyah, a sect that halted their belief in the Imamate at Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim (d. 99 AH), claiming he did not die but remained hidden. The text emphasizes his intense enmity toward the subsequent Imams, particularly Imam ʿAlī al-Riḍā, marking the schism between those who accepted the continuation of the Imamate and those who 'stopped' at the seventh Imam. This biographical note serves as a critical reference for understanding the early theological disputes regarding the death and succession of the Imams in Shia history.
en.seo_question: Who was Ali ibn Abi Hamza and why is he considered the root of the Waqf sect?

key_terms.الْوَقْفِ: Waqf (the state of stopping/remaining, referring to the Waqifiyyah sect)
